name: IRS20957STRPBF
title: Protected half-bridge MOSFET driver for class D audio, 200 V
summary: The IRS20957S drives the two MOSFETs of a class D audio half bridge from a PWM signal. Its PWM input stage runs from its own floating supply, VDD to VSS, which can sit from 0 to 100 V above COM. Over-current is detected for load current of either sign without a shunt resistor, and a capacitor on CSD programs the protection reset timer. Dead time is one of four preset values, picked by the voltage on DT.
key_figures: +/- 100 V (VS up to 200 V above COM)

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: A class D half bridge on split rails +B and -B. COM sits at -B and a 12 V supply above -B feeds VCC; the floating input stage is referenced to ground at VSS and fed from +B through a resistor, with VDD clamped by the internal zener. Two N-channel MOSFETs, each with a gate resistor, form the bridge; VB is charged from VCC through a bootstrap diode. CSH watches the high side drain through a resistor network, with a blocking diode to +B and a resistor to VB. A divider from VCC sets DT, and a resistor from VREF with one to COM sets OCSET. The switch node drives the speaker through an LC low-pass filter.

operation.text: Three supplies: VDD-VSS for the floating PWM input, VCC-COM for the low side and logic, and VB-VS for the high side. Each has an internal shunt zener, clamping at 10.2 V, 20.4 V and 15.3 V typ, each rated for 10 mA. The recommended VDD clamp current is 1 to 5 mA; in the typical connection VDD is fed from +B through a resistor.

The PWM input stage runs from VDD-VSS, with VSS from 0 to 100 V above COM recommended and VDD rated to 210 V absolute. IN takes 3.3 V or 5 V logic referenced to VSS. Propagation delays are 95 ns on and 80 ns off typ with VSS floating at 100 V and with VSS tied to COM.
Each supply has its own UVLO: VCC turns on at 8.9 V and off at 8.7 V typ, VBS at 8.5 and 8.3 V, VDD at 8.7 and 8.2 V.

Dead time is generated inside and picked by the DT voltage against fractions of VCC: 15, 25, 35 or 80 ns typ. Each value applies to both LO-off-to-HO-on and HO-off-to-LO-on. In the typical connection a resistor divider from VCC to COM sets DT.

Over-current is detected for load current of either sign with no shunt resistor. The low side threshold is a VS voltage set by OCSET (1.2 V typ at OCSET = 1.2 V); OCSET is set from VREF through resistors, with 6.3 to 16.7 kΩ in total from VREF. The high side threshold is CSH at 1.2 V typ above VS. In the typical connection CSH reaches the high side drain through a resistor and a diode, with a resistor up to VB. From a threshold crossing to the output turning off takes 500 ns max.

A capacitor from CSD to VSS sets the timing of the protection sequence and its reset timer; CSD charges and discharges at 100 µA typ. Its two thresholds are the shutdown release level, 0.70 × VDD typ, and the self reset level, 0.30 × VDD typ. CSD falling through Vth1 turns the outputs off within 250 ns max.
VS and VSS may slew at up to 50 V/ns; at power-up VSS may rise at up to 50 V/ms.
The top carries the IR logo, the part number, a date code (YWW) with a marking code letter (P for lead-free), a pin 1 dot, an assembly site code and a lot code.
